result.title: Degree-Equalized View-Graph Selection under Tight Pair Budgets
result.summary: Fully matching all image pairs in Structure-from-Motion is quadratic in the number of images, so practical pipelines pass a budgeted subset to the final matching and reconstruction backend. One-shot selectors score candidates with image retrieval, cheap geometric probes, or a learned prior and finalize B pairs before full matching. Their priorities do not account for the degree already allocated to each image, which can concentrate edges on a few images. Across nine large 1DSfM internet photo collections at B=2N, the coverage top-B selector leaves 54% of covered images with realized degree at most two. Reconstruction can then fail even when the selected graph is nearly connected and almost fully verified. Our training-free greedy rule, Degree-Equalized Allocation (DEAL), exponentially downweights pairs whose endpoints are already well covered. On these collections, DEAL improves the one-shot selector built on the same prior (from 0.776 to 0.929) and matches the mean registered-image ratio of an SfM-supervised edge prior under the shared backend (0.929 vs 0.930), without training. On the largely saturated 38-scene standard benchmark suite, DEAL gives the highest mean among the evaluated training-free selectors (0.875 vs 0.858 one-shot).

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 Structure-from-Motion 在严格图像对预算下如何一次性挑选进入完整匹配的视图图边，提出无需训练的贪心规则 DEAL，对端点已被充分覆盖的候选对做指数降权，在九个 1DSfM 集合与标准基准上提升配准图像比例。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按已分配预算均衡覆盖、避免证据集中于少数项」的分配准则，可能为 LVR 中在有限计算下筛选待验证视觉证据、评估覆盖失衡导致的失败提供可核查的思路，但与原论文的推理状态机制无直接关联。
